cells.tense: Here, in this hour, you are steering and the steering is yours.
cells.act: keep it at its real size when you are asked to shrink it
cells.ask: When a room or a mood wants your aim made smaller, don't shrink it. Keep it the actual size while the pressure's on. No tightening, no bracing — just hold the size.
cells.core:
You can point yourself at something and mean it. That's the whole move: not force, just the plain ability to say this and not that, and have your energy follow the sentence. When the aim is clean it doesn't feel like pushing. It feels like being where you already decided to be, and the decision holds without being remade every hour.

Where this is holding now, the direction comes from the present, not from something you're outrunning. That's worth noticing, because you'll be asked to shrink it soon. Keep it the size it actually is when someone wants it smaller. Don't tighten, don't brace — just don't shrink. The steering is yours, and nothing about it needs proving.
cells.sheetLine: You can point yourself somewhere and mean it.
cells.verb: Directing energy toward a chosen end

cells.tense: You are already bracing for an outcome you cannot write in yet.
cells.act: see the whole pattern you are standing inside
cells.ask: Before the next push, stop and take in the whole arrangement around what you're forcing — where you sit in it, what the other parts are doing. Sketch it if that helps. See it whole once before you move again.
cells.core:
When the aim runs ahead of now, it turns into grip. You're managing an outcome that hasn't happened, tightening around a version of next week that doesn't exist yet, and the tightening reads as control — to you, to anyone near it. The aiming itself is fine. It's just projected forward, white-knuckling something that hasn't arrived.

What returns you isn't pushing less; it's seeing more. Look at the whole arrangement you're standing inside before you act in it again. You don't need to know how it ends — just take in the whole shape, including your place in it. Knowing it that way deepens instead of closing. This week, look longer instead of harder, and treat one long look as the day's real work.
cells.sheetLine: The bracing is you writing next week in advance.
cells.verb: Directing energy toward a chosen end

cells.tense: You are standing at a door that closed behind you already.
cells.act: do the thing in your own way, without proving it
cells.ask: Whatever you reach for today, do it your own way and skip the proof. No defending, no showing anyone it was right. Just your hand doing its own work, unshown.
cells.core:
The aim isn't broken. It's gone quiet. Somewhere you stopped pointing at things, and the silence reads as 'what's the point' — not laziness, just a hand that went still a while back and hasn't picked up the pen since. The door you're facing isn't the one ahead of you; it's the one behind, and you're still turned toward it.

This comes back in small moves. Whatever you do today, do it your own way and skip the proving — not a pitch, not a performance, just your own hand doing its own thing. That's what returns charge to what's running low. It doesn't argue you back into direction. It just shows you where your own way already lives, and lets it show unannounced.
cells.sheetLine: The direction went quiet. It didn't leave.
cells.verb: Directing energy toward a chosen end

cells.tense: You are already writing, and your hand calls it just how things go.
cells.act: put your own name on what is already yours
cells.ask: Take the course you're on and quietly own that you set it — no story about how it happened, just the plain fact that the steering is yours. Carry on after.
cells.core:
You're moving in a course you'd describe as momentum, or habit, or just how the year turned out. The steering is real. The hand is on it. But if someone asked who decided, you'd point at circumstance — and the choices are good ones, they're just filed under something else, so the hand on the wheel slips out of view.

It comes back by naming. Take the course you're already on and acknowledge, to yourself, that you set it — no one else needs to hear it. Not a plan, not a justification, just the plain fact that the direction carries your mark. When the wheel is visibly in your hands, the same motion stops feeling like drift.
cells.sheetLine: The direction carries your mark. Calling it momentum is what hides that.
cells.verb: Directing energy toward a chosen end
